subject: Atlas Logistics — POC ops playbook, success criteria & access
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@atlaslogistics.com>, Dan Brooks <dan.brooks@atlaslogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Atlas Logistics — POC ops playbook, success criteria & access

Hi Claire / Dan —

Great to meet you both this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear ownership for the POC: 

Call recap (30m):
- Goal: Validate Redwood Inference as the low-latency, cost-effective inference layer for Atlas internal search and document summarization workflows.
- Scope: 2-week POC covering: relevance (search) for 3k-doc dataset, summarization quality on shipment notes, and 95th%-tile latency under expected query load (preview infra).

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Relevance: MRR >= 0.60 on our benchmark prompts (we'll exchange prompt set)
2) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms for median prompt length (~120 tokens) under 15 QPS sustained
3) Cost/throughput: baseline token cost estimate within 15% of the forecast we gave; identify optimization levers (quantization, batching)
4) Security: SSO for team members + IP allowlist for the pilot environment; no customer PII to be retained in logs (retention = 0 days by default)

Immediate asks / owners / target dates:
- Atlas: provide list of 4 pilot reviewers + emails for SSO invites (Claire) — due: Tue, Nov 25
- Atlas: complete the network allowlist section (we attached a template) if IP blocks required (Dan) — due: Mon, Nov 24
- Redwood: provision a sandbox API key (scoped, short-lived) and an SSO invite for pilot users (Neha) — target: Wed, Nov 26
- Redwood: push the initial evaluation dataset & sample prompts to our shared Drive and provide a short quickstart README (Rishi) — target: Wed, Nov 26

Attachments: I attached a brief scoping sheet and a network-allowlist template to make the IP step quick.

Next step: Would you like us to schedule a 30-min engineering sync (network + auth) this week or early next week? I can propose times.

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@atlaslogistics.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Atlas Logistics — POC ops playbook, success criteria & access

Thanks Neha — very helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Success criteria: MRR target sounds right; for latency, our internal SLA for designer-facing tools is 250ms at 95th, but for this pilot we can accept up to 300ms as a practical target. Please flag any tradeoffs so we can prioritize accuracy vs latency.

2) Data: We'll supply a redacted 3k-doc set and the prompt set by Monday. That dataset will not include customer identifying info, but some shipment notes contain internal IDs — we'll mark those as non-sensitive.

3) Access: For SSO we use Okta. Can you confirm SAML metadata or do you prefer SCIM for provisioning? We prefer SCIM if possible to streamline invites.

4) Network: Our infra team needs an exact list of outbound IP ranges that Redwood will use for the sandbox so they can add to the allowlist. Dan, can you pick this up?

We'd like an engineering sync Thursday if you have availability.

Claire Zhang
Principal Product Manager — Search
Atlas Logistics
c.zhang@atlaslogistics.com

On Thu, Nov 20, 2025 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Atlas Logistics — POC ops playbook, success criteria & access

Thanks Claire — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Latency vs accuracy tradeoffs: we'll start with the medium-latency configuration to hit ~300ms 95th; if you need 250ms we can move to a lower-latency setup but it will increase cost ~20-30% or require a smaller context size. We'll run both profiles during the POC and report metrics.

2) Data: perfect — please drop the redacted set in the shared Drive link I just pushed to HubSpot. We'll run the same prompt set across our eval harness.

3) SSO / provisioning: Redwood supports both SAML and SCIM. SCIM will allow us to push users from Atlas Okta to the pilot tenant (recommended). If you prefer SAML-only we can issue invites manually. Please confirm which you prefer; if SCIM, please share a technical contact for Okta integration.

4) Network: attached template includes the outbound IP list for the sandbox environment. Our sandbox uses a small set of egress IPs; we'll provide an exact CIDR list after the engineering sync.

Proposed schedule:
- Mon Nov 24: Atlas provides filled scoping sheet + pilot reviewer emails (Claire)
- Wed Nov 26: Redwood provisions sandbox & SCIM connector; short quickstart + API key (Neha / Rishi)
- Thu Nov 27: 30-min sync to run through network, SSO, and evaluation measurement plan (all)

Action items (owners):
- Claire: confirm SCIM vs SAML and provide Okta contact (due Mon Nov 24)
- Dan: complete allowlist template with any corporate egress blocks (due Mon Nov 24)
- Neha: provision scoped sandbox API key and coordinate SSO/SCIM setup (target Wed Nov 26)
- Rishi: share quickstart and initial eval harness steps (target Wed Nov 26)

I'll pencil the Thu 27 slot and send a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Best,
Neha
